Hello in this report I will be going over the following 5 analysis methods: Moving Averages, Moving Average Convergence Divergence, Fibonacci Retracement, Bollinger Bands & Relative Strength Index. 

The Moving Averages analysis method attempts to determine the trend of a stock's price by using the average price of the stock over a period of time. In this case, the Moving Average is calculated by taking the average of the stock's closing prices. This analysis method can be more useful as the length of the period increases. The score for this method is 5 out of 10.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) analysis method is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between the short-term and long-term moving averages of a stock's price. The MACD is calculated by subtracting the 26-day exponential moving average (EMA) from the 12-day EMA. The MACD can be used to identify bullish and bearish trends, as well as to generate buy and sell signals. It has a score of 2 out of 10.

The Fibonacci Retracement analysis method is a technical analysis tool that is used to identify potential support and resistance levels in a stock's price. The Fibonacci Retracement is based on the idea that a stock's price will often retrace a certain percentage of its previous move. This method has a score of 4 out of 10.

The Bollinger Bands analysis method is a volatility indicator that shows the range of a stock's price relative to its moving average. The Bollinger Bands are calculated by adding and subtracting two standard deviations from the 20-day moving average of a stock's price. The Bollinger Bands can be used to identify overbought and oversold conditions. It has a score of 3 out of 10.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) analysis method is a momentum indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or overbought conditions in an asset. The RSI is calculated by measuring the ratio of the average of the last n-days' closes that were higher than the previous day's close, to the average of the last n-days' closes that were lower than the previous day's close. It has a score of 9 out of 10.

Overall, the RSI is the most positive of the indicators, suggesting momentum and potential buy conditions. 

As the RSI is the strongest indicator, with the rest being neutral or negative, the overall trend is neutral, with a risk level of 1 out of 5. The overall risk is low. The decision is HOLD.
